findings.claim: The change filters ALL analyzer diagnostics whose location is not in the compilation, a behavior shift beyond guarding the three index sites. This matches the deliberate policy that metadata types are not analysed and get no diagnostics, so dropping them is consistent with the ledger.

receipt_plan.detail: [L12] Types from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostics; suppressing diagnostics for metadata symbols is not a defect.

findings.claim: Unrelated change in the serializer runtime: the `case <= byte.MaxValue` branch is removed from the unsigned-int writer, so values 128..255 now encode as UInt16 (0xcd) instead of UInt8 (0xcc). This changes wire bytes, is non-canonical and larger, and has nothing to do with REQ-2283. Ledger L13 notes numeric serialization is bug-prone.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize uint/ulong/int values 128..255 (e.g. 200) with the base-built and head-built MessagePack and compare bytes: base emits CC C8, head emits CD 00 C8. Also run the MessagePackWriter/primitives tests for the UInt8 boundary.

findings.claim: Docs added to README and MsgPack004.md describe a diagnostics-ownership policy for referenced assemblies. The README text is inexact: it says diagnostics about members of such types are reported by the defining assembly, but the change only drops them. The README section also sits under the custom-formatters area rather than a generics section, and no analyzer release note is needed since no diagnostic was added.

receipt_plan.detail: Read README.md lines 1636-1643 and compare them to ReportIfLocatedInCompilation; the claim that the defining assembly reports the diagnostics holds only if that assembly also runs the analyzer.
